Dear Secretary Reese:

           Pursuant to section 205 of the Federal Power Act (“FPA”)1 and Part 35 of the rules and

regulations of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“Commission” or “FERC”),2 PJM

Interconnection, L.L.C. (“PJM”) hereby submits proposed revisions (“Proposed Revisions”) to the

PJM Open Access Transmission Tariff (“Tariff”) to establish a pro forma reliability must run

service agreement (“RMR Agreement”) and modify existing rules that will account for resources

that operate under the pro forma RMR Agreement. PJM respectfully requests that the Commission

issue an order on this filing by no later than December 14, 2026, and accept the Proposed

Revisions, including the pro forma RMR Agreement, contained herein effective December 15,

2026. This proposal represents the cumulation of a collaborative stakeholder process that was

ultimately endorsed by the PJM Members Committee by acclamation with two abstentions and

three objections on August 19, 2026.

 I.         INTRODUCTION AND SUMMARY

           The resource mix in PJM is undergoing a rapid transition due, in part, to a significant

portion of PJM’s dispatchable generation fleet retiring, or entering the process of retiring, in

response to a mix of state and federal policies. As PJM reported in 2023, approximately 40 GW

of generation in PJM is at risk of retirement before 2030.3 While the pace of resource retirements

has somewhat slowed in recent years, this has been offset by the rapid load growth from increased

demand for data centers and other large loads. This, combined with the relatively slow arrival of

replacement resources, has resulted in an extreme and rapid imbalance of supply and demand.

           In response to this load growth, PJM revised several aspects of its capacity market, the

Reliability Pricing Model (“RPM”),4 to adapt to the rapidly tightening supply and demand

conditions expected to continue into future auctions.5 Among those revisions, PJM proposed an

interim solution whereby it would use an objective criteria to consider the capacity capability of

an RMR Resource toward meeting PJM’s capacity reliability requirements for the 2026/2027 and

2027/2028 Delivery Years.6 PJM determined that RMR Resources that met those criteria could

perform during capacity emergencies similar to a committed Capacity Resource and proposed to

administratively include those RMR Resources into the supply stack for the Base Residual

            PJM’s current process allows an RMR Resource to continue operating based on resource-

performance and availability requirements. Due to the lack of uniformity in these requirements,

PJM does not categorically account for all RMR Resources as capacity necessary to meet the

region’s reliability needs under the current RMR process.

             Through this filing, the proposed revisions to the Tariff, including the pro forma RMR

Agreement, are designed to provide greater uniformity as to the obligation of RMR Resources.

Among other things, the RMR Agreement provides clear standards establishing the term of the

RMR Agreement, clarifies and limits the reasons for termination of the RMR Agreement by both

the Generation Owner and PJM, details when PJM may schedule and dispatch the applicable RMR

Resource, and specifies the means by which a Generation Owner may elect to receive

compensation for the provision of RMR Service. As further described below, the terms of the pro

forma RMR Agreement, as well as Proposed Revisions to the Tariff, are just and reasonable and

not unduly discriminatory or preferential.

II.         BACKGROUND

            A.       PJM’s Current Deactivation Rules

            PJM’s generator deactivation rules are set forth in Part V of the Tariff. Generation Owners

who wish to deactivate their generator must provide notice of the proposed Deactivation in writing

to PJM at least 12 months before the desired Deactivation Date.12 Following receipt of the

Generation Owner’s notice, PJM determines whether Deactivation would “adversely affect the

reliability of the Transmission System.”13 If there are no reliability issues associated with the

proposed Deactivation, PJM will notify the Generation Owner, who may deactivate its generating

unit any time thereafter.14 If there are transmission reliability issues identified due to proposed

Deactivation, the Generation Owner may still choose to deactivate its generating unit.15

Notwithstanding, a Generation Owner may elect to operate its generator under an RMR agreement

impact resulting from Deactivation of the generator are constructed.

               Under the current RMR framework, the Generation Owner with the deactivating generator

may decide: (1) whether the resource elects to remain in operation after the Deactivation Date to

address transmission reliability issues; (2) how the RMR Resource may operate during the retained

period (in accordance with terms negotiated with PJM); and (3) the means by which the RMR

Resource may be compensated, i.e., whether through the Deactivation Avoidable Cost Credit16 or

through a cost of service rate to recover the entire cost of operating the generating unit until

Deactivation.17 As a result, the terms and conditions under which each retained RMR Resource

agrees to stay online and operate are currently both situation and resource-specific. The operating

terms are negotiated with PJM on a case-by-case basis and subject to Commission review, which

can take significant time to conclude. Thus, each RMR Resource can be subject to varying

performance requirements. For example, some RMR agreements call for RMR Resources to

perform during “capacity emergencies,”18 while other agreements have not.19 This has necessarily

led to inconsistencies and a lack of predictability even though a generator operating under an RMR

           B.        Summary of the Proposed Pro Forma RMR Agreement and Proposed
                     Revisions to the Tariff

           The purpose of this proceeding is to establish a pro forma RMR Agreement and necessary

tariff revisions that will set standardized terms and conditions for RMR Resources, expedite the

retention of those resources, and allow such RMR Resources to be counted towards meeting PJM’s

capacity needs. This filing presents a just and reasonable and not unduly discriminatory or

preferential solution to inconsistent RMR service resulting from the lack of a pro forma RMR

agreement in the PJM Tariff.

           The Proposed Revisions, including the pro forma RMR Agreement, significantly improve

the efficiency and efficacy of PJM’s RMR program. The RMR Agreement allows PJM to retain

deactivating generators expeditiously by eliminating the need to submit each RMR Agreement

under FPA section 205 and by reducing the time spent negotiating the terms of the RMR

Agreement from scratch. Instead, RMR Resources that adopt the pro forma RMR Agreement will

only need to make a filing under FPA section 205 if they pursue the cost-of-service rate under

Tariff, Part V, section 119.21 This ability to quickly retain RMR Resources is a crucial bolster to

reliability given that, as of 2023, 40 GW of generation was at risk of retirement by 2030.22 While

Generation Owners and PJM are allowed to include unit-specific provisions in the pro forma

agreement,23 this proposal will nonetheless reduce the issues that come before the Commission.

            Even in the case that the Commission is required to review an RMR Agreement under its

nonconforming agreement standard, its review will now be limited to considering the

compensation component and any additional material changes from the form RMR Agreement, if

any. That will reduce the scope and frequency of disputes, which can take years to resolve if

aggrieved parties seek rehearing and judicial review. Thus, the RMR Agreement and Proposed

Revisions will result in similarly situated generators being treated similarly by applying the same

terms and conditions to all RMR Resources as a baseline.

           One specific concern that may be raised by potential protestors is that a Generation Owner

may elect to adopt the RMR Agreement but not be able to recoup its costs if the Commission were

to reject their cost-of-service rate application. Those concerns are unfounded. The Commission

will ultimately accept a just and reasonable rate that compensates Generation Owners for retaining

their generating units.24 Hypothetical arguments that the Commission may impose a confiscatory

rate are speculative at best and certainly do not form a basis for rejecting a Section 205 application

designed to provide a more efficient and uniform process for addressing RMR designations.

Further, the cost-of-service rate is only one of two available compensation methods. Generation

Owners may also pursue the Deactivation Avoidable Cost Credit methodology which has been

approved by the Commission as just and reasonable and, as such, only requires an information

filing, as an alternative to the cost-of-service rate.25 Finally, RMR unit owners would still have

access to the courts to address any action by the Commission the unit owner deems confiscatory.

        C.       Stakeholder Process

        The Proposed Revisions, including the pro forma RMR Agreement, received broad support

from PJM’s stakeholders. The Deactivation Enhancements Senior Task Force endorsed this

proposal with 53% support. Subsequently, a supermajority of PJM stakeholders endorsed this

proposal at the Markets and Reliability Committee with a sector weighted tally of 4.068 out of 5

on July 28, 2026. Finally, the Members Committee endorsed this proposal by acclamation with

two abstentions and three objections on August 19, 2026.

III.    SUMMARY OF THE FORM RMR AGREEMENT

        The RMR Agreement contains just and reasonable terms for securing the performance of

RMR Resources. The proposed RMR Agreement is comparable to other pro forma RMR

Agreements that the Commission has previously accepted as just and reasonable from four of the

six RTOs/ISOs.26 It provides a predictable framework for addressing reliability needs while

reducing uncertainty to Market Participants, stakeholders, and federal and state regulators, and the

Commission should find it just and reasonable as it has other RTO/ISO pro forma RMR

agreements. Those specific proposed RMR Agreement terms are summarized below.

               1.      Section 1.0: Definitions

       Section 1 sets forth the definitions governing the RMR Agreement and establishes that,

except as otherwise defined in the RMR Agreement, capitalized terms will have the same meaning

established under PJM’s Tariff, Operating Agreement, and the RAA.

              2.      Section 2.0: Effective Date

       Section 2.0 provides that the RMR Agreement is contingent on the Commission’s

acceptance and will become effective on the date agreed to by the parties or specified by the

Commission.

              3.      Section 2.1: Term

       Section 2.1 states that the term of the RMR Agreement will commence on the Effective

Date and will end on the Anticipated In-Service Date of Transmission Upgrades, provided that the

term may be terminated prior to, or extended beyond, the Term. If PJM has administratively

included the RMR Resource in an RPM Auction under Tariff, Attachment DD, Section 5.3(b), the

Term will end on the later of the Anticipated In-Service Date of Transmission Upgrades or the

conclusion of the Delivery Year in which the RMR Resource is administratively included in an

RPM Auction.

              4.      Section 2.2: Termination by Generation Owner

       Section 2.2 sets forth the means by which a Generation Owner may terminate the RMR

Agreement with respect to the entire RMR Resource or specific units. The Generation Owner may

terminate the RMR Agreement upon occurrence of a Catastrophic Force Majeure or if PJM does

not approve a properly submitted Project Investment (i.e., an investment made by the Generation

Owner to enable continuing operations for the period identified as having a reliability need for the

RMR Resource) that is necessary to continue operating the RMR Resource to provide RMR

Service for the Term. In either case, Generation Owner will provide prompt written notice to PJM



                                                 9
 and the Market Monitoring Unit (“IMM”) of its intent to terminate the RMR Agreement as soon

as reasonably practical. Termination will be effective 61 days after the RMR Resource becomes

inoperable by virtue of the Catastrophic Force Majeure, or by virtue of PJM not approving Project

Investment necessary for the continued operation of the RMR Resource to provide RMR Service.

              5.       Section 2.3: Termination by PJM

       Section 2.3 states that PJM may terminate the RMR Agreement upon determining that the

RMR Resource is no longer necessary and after providing the Generation Owner and the IMM

with written notice.

              6.       Section 2.4: Effect of Termination

       Section 2.4 explains that termination of the RMR Agreement will not relieve the

Generation Owner of its obligations as a PJM Member under the Operating Agreement or Tariff,

nor will termination reduce PJM’s ability to pursue remedies against the Generation Owner under

the Operating Agreement or Tariff, or PJM’s ability to submit an application under FPA section

202(c). Termination will not relieve either Party of any obligation or remedy arising during the

effective period of the RMR Agreement.

              7.       Section 2.5: Extension

       Section 2.5 sets forth the procedures for extending the Term of the RMR Agreement. PJM

will first submit a written request to the Generation Owner proposing to extend the Term. Within

14 days after receipt of PJM’s written request, and no less than three days prior to the conclusion

of the Term, Generation Owner will provide written notice to PJM that it will either accept the

extended Term, or that it cannot accept the extended Term because the Generation Owner is not

capable of continuing to provide RMR Service for the extended Term. Among other things, this

provision specifies that the Generator Owner will not enter into any contracts, agreements, or

settlements, or take any other action, which would prevent extension of the Term.

               8.     Section 3.0: Use of Market Resources Prior to RMR Resource

       Section 3.0 states that before scheduling and dispatching the RMR Resource, PJM will first

examine the use of available economic generation resources to address the applicable reliability

concern. PJM will not be required to call an emergency in order to schedule or dispatch the RMR

Resource.

              9.     Section 3.1: Scheduling and Dispatch of RMR Resource

       Section 3.1 provides that PJM may schedule and dispatch the RMR Resource, when, in its

sole determination and engineering judgment, scheduling and dispatch is necessary to address four

circumstances: (A) transmission facilities within the PJM Region are at risk of not being operated

within thermal, voltage, and stability limits established under PJM Manual 3; (B) a transmission

reliability need caused by a system restoration, effectuated in accordance with PJM Manual 36;

(C) a projected or actual capacity emergency, as described in PJM Manual 13, during which PJM

determines that the resources scheduled and available for a specific Operating Day may not be

sufficient to maintain appropriate reserve levels for the PJM Region; or (D) the RMR Resource

needs to perform any required operational testing. Generation Owner must operate the RMR

Resource upon receipt of, and consistent with, any scheduling or dispatch instruction issued by

PJM subject to limitations specified in Sections 3.2 and 3.3 of the RMR Agreement.

              10.    Section 3.2: Offering RMR Resource Into PJM Markets

       Section 3.2 states, among other things, that when not scheduled or dispatched by PJM, the

Generation Owner will offer the RMR Resource into the Day-ahead Energy Market and the Real-

time Energy Market via Markets Gateway, using the status “Unavailable” and a corresponding

eDART ticket indicating that the RMR Resource is available to run if requested by PJM. PJM will

utilize the applicable cost-based schedule when dispatching the RMR Resource. The Generation

Owner shall enter and update in Markets Gateway any applicable unit parameters or operational



                                               11
 limitations in order to accurately reflect the operating condition of the RMR Resource. The

Generation Owner will submit an eDART ticket for any outage, planned maintenance work, or

unplanned maintenance work, and use best efforts to submit any planned outage as far in advance

as practicable. During the Term of the RMR Agreement, the Generation Owner will not offer the

RMR Resource into RPM Auctions, and will not be subject to penalties arising under the RPM

Auctions for operation of the RMR Resource.

                   11.      Section 3.3: Operational Obligations and Commitments

           Section 3.3 provides that PJM will not issue scheduling or dispatch instruction to

Generation Owner during periods when the RMR Resource is operationally unavailable due to an

outage or maintenance work. The Generation Owner will not be obligated to cause the RMR

Resource to be operated in a manner that will cause the Generation Owner to violate any applicable

federal, state, or local law or regulation, including but not limited to any applicable environmental,

emissions or permit requirements.27 Among other things, Section 3.3 further provides that the

Generation Owner will undertake best efforts to cost-effectively ensure the availability of fuel,

equipment, parts, and/or any other inputs necessary to the production of electric energy and that

the Generation Owner will operate the RMR Resource consistent with Good Utility Practice. The

Generation Owner is not required to guarantee that the RMR Resource will be available for

operation upon receipt of a PJM scheduling or dispatch instruction, nor is the Generation Owner

required to guarantee that the RMR Resource will operate at its rated capacity.

                   12.      Section 4.0: Generation Owner Election and PJM Payment Obligation

           Section 4.0 states that Generation Owner may elect to receive compensation for the

provision of RMR Service either through the Deactivation Avoidable Cost Credit, or alternatively

Commission under Tariff, section 119 and FPA section 205. PJM will compensate the Generation

              13.    Section 5.0: Invoicing

       Section 5.0 provides that the Generation Owner will issue a monthly invoice to PJM, with

a copy to the IMM, for the amounts due under Section 4 of the RMR Agreement no later than the

15th calendar day of the month, following the month in which RMR Service is provided. Upon

applicable to items on the invoice. PJM will credit any and all monthly net revenues generated

from any sales by the RMR Resource of wholesale energy and ancillary services under the PJM

Tariff, Operating Agreement, or RAA, identified on the applicable monthly PJM bill, against the

charges paid to the Generation Owner for RMR Service. Any positive net revenues that exceed

the charges in a given month will transfer to the following month’s bill and will be available for

use as a credit against any future charges under Section 4 of the RMR Agreement for the duration

of the Term. At the end of the Term, PJM will credit any remaining net positive revenues that

exceed the total charges under Section 4 to Generation Owner.

              14.    Section 5.1: Billing

       Section 5.1 states, among other things, that PJM will include the charges invoiced by the

Generation Owner in the PJM monthly billing statement for the month in which PJM received the

invoice from the Generation Owner (for example, if the April invoice is received by PJM in May,

those charges will become part of the PJM monthly bill for May). If the Generation Owner does

not remit the invoice to PJM in accordance with the timeline specified in Section 5.0 of the RMR

Agreement, PJM will include the charges in the PJM monthly billing statement by no later than

the month following the month in which the Generation Owner remits the invoice to PJM.

               15.    Section 6.0: Representations of PJM

       Section 6.0 sets forth PJM’s representations to the Generation Owner regarding PJM’s

valid existence, power and authority to perform its obligations, necessary regulatory

authorizations, and confirmation that the RMR Agreement does not violate the Tariff, Operating

Agreement, or RAA, any contracts or agreement to which PJM is a party, or any law applicable to

PJM.

              16.    Section 6.1: Representations of Generation Owner

       Section 6.1 provides the Generation Owner’s representations regarding its valid existence,

satisfaction of all applicable PJM credit requirements under Tariff, Attachment Q, regulatory

authorizations, performance, etc.

              17.    Section 7.0: PJM Settlements, Inc.

       Section 7.0 provides that PJM may utilize its subsidiary PJM Settlements, Inc. to perform

any of the functions or obligations established in the RMR Agreement.

              18.    Section 7.1: Scheduler or Energy Manager

       Section 7.1 states that the Generation Owner may utilize a third-party schedule or energy

manager to perform, on the Generation Owner’s behalf, any of the Generation Owner’s obligations

under the RMR Agreement, so long as the energy manager is identified in Section 8 of the RMR

Agreement.

              19.    Section 7.2: Preservation of Rights Under the PJM Tariff and Operating
                     Agreement

       Section 7.2 explains that the Parties mutually acknowledge that the RMR Agreement is

entered into pursuant to Part V of PJM’s Tariff and Operating Agreement and that the rights and

obligations set forth in those documents are fully preserved. Breach of the RMR Agreement will

constitute a violation and/or breach of the Tariff, Operating Agreement, and/or both.




                                               14
                20.     Section 7.3: Waiver

        Section 7.3 states that the Parties may, by mutual agreement, waive any of the time periods

in the RMR Agreement that apply to PJM and the Generation Owner. It further provides that

failure to exercise any remedy or to enforce any right will not constitute a waiver of that remedy

or right or of any other remedy or rights. A Party will only be considered to have waived any

remedies or rights if that waiver is set forth in writing.

               21.     Section 7.4: No Third-Party Beneficiaries

        Section 7.4 explains that except as set forth in the RMR Agreement, nothing in the RMR

Agreement confers any rights or remedies under, or by reason of, the RMR Agreement on any

persons other than the Parties and their respective successors and assigns, nor is anything in the

RMR Agreement intended to relieve or discharge the obligations or liability of any third party, nor

give any third party any rights of subrogation or action against a Party.

               22.     Section 7.5: Transfer of RMR Resource

        Section 7.5 provides that the Generation Owner will not sell or transfer the RMR Resource

to a different entity during the Term unless (A) authorized by the Commission under FPA section

203; (B) the Generation Owner and the Purchaser of the RMR Resource comply with all

requirements under PJM Manual 14D related to generation transfers; (C) the Purchaser satisfies

all applicable credit requirements under Tariff, Attachment Q; (D) the Purchaser executes the

Operating Agreement and becomes a PJM Member; (E) the Generation Owner assigns the RMR

Agreement to the Purchaser, and the Purchaser agrees, in writing, to assume the RMR Agreement

as the assignee and to perform all of Generation Owner’s obligations under the RMR Agreement;

and (F) PJM provides written authorization for the transfer, which will not be unreasonably

withheld.

                    23.      Section 8.0: Designated Representatives

           Section 8.0 states the means of providing notice to the Parties and sets forth the names and

contact information of each Party’s designated representatives.

                   24.      Section 9.0: Signatures

           Section 9.0 sets forth the signature blocks of the Parties to the RMR Agreement.

                   25.      Appendices

           Appendices A and B include unit-specific characteristics and any special provisions

necessary to implement the RMR Agreement. Special provisions that do not contradict the text or

purpose of the Form RMR Agreement will be treated as conforming provisions that do not require

filing with the Commission.

IV.        EXPLANATION OF PROPOSED REVISIONS TO THE TARIFF

           A.       Changes to Tariff, Attachment DD, Section 5.3

           PJM proposes to revise Tariff, Attachment DD, section 5.3 to expand the applicability of

section 5.3(b) to any Generation Capacity Resource retained through the pro forma RMR

Agreement. More particularly, the amendments make clear that a Generation Capacity Resource

will be included in the Base Residual Auction as a price taker (i.e., $0/MW-Day) if it is retained

through the pro forma RMR Agreement and that is subject to the Deactivation Avoidable Cost

Credit or a cost of service revenue requirement submitted to and accepted by the Commission for

the relevant Delivery Year at least three months prior to the posting of the planning parameters.28

To the extent there is an increase in Accredited UCAP, the additional MWs will also be included

in the Third Incremental Auction with a Sell Offer of $0/MW-day.29




28

29

            Prior to these proposed amendments, Tariff, Attachment DD, section 5.3(b) was applicable

to Generation Capacity Resources retained to address transmission reliability and that (1) did not

clear an RPM Auction for the relevant Delivery Year based on an offer submitted by the Capacity

Market Seller and (2) were the subject of a rate schedule satisfying certain requirements. The

proposed amendments expand this section to include RMR Resources operating under the pro

forma RMR Agreement that satisfies the requirements of Tariff, Attachment DD, section

5.3(b)(i)(I). Additionally, such RMR Resources will need to be reasonably expected to (A) be

deliverable and able to operate during the relevant Delivery Year and not prohibited from operating

during the relevant Delivery Year based on any bilateral restrictions with any private third-party

entity; and (B) be available for dispatch by the Office of the Interconnection in expectation of any

PJM emergencies and to address emergencies absent the resource being on an outage.30 The pro

forma RMR Agreement satisfies these expectations. Specifically, Section 3.1 of the RMR

Agreement provides that PJM may schedule and dispatch the RMR Resource when necessary to

address certain scenarios, including a “projected or actual capacity emergency.” Section 3.3 of the

RMR Agreement further requires a Generation Owner to “at all times prepare, maintain, and

operate the RMR Resource consistent with Good Utility Practice, so that the RMR Resource can

be reasonably expected to be able to operate for the entire Term of this Agreement” and to “ensure

that the RMR Resource continues to meet the deliverability requirements under RAA, Schedule

10, and maintain sufficient Capacity Interconnection Rights to safely inject the output of the RMR

Resource into the Transmission System.” The Generation Owner that is party to an RMR

Agreement must also represent that it has full power and authority to perform all of its duties,

obligations, representations, and covenants under the RMR Agreement and to operate, maintain,



30
     Proposed Tariff, Attachment DD, section 5.3(b).



                                                       17
 and administer the RMR Resource.31 The Generation Owner likewise represents that performance

of the RMR Agreement does not violate the terms and conditions of any contracts to which it is

party.32

            The Proposed Revisions retain all other provisions of Tariff, Attachment DD, section 5.3

that apply to Generation Owners that accept the RMR Agreement. Thus, if the RMR Resources

Accredited UCAP is higher than the amount offered in the Base Residual Auction where the RMR

Resource was the subject of a Sell Offer, the additional Accredited UCAP will be offered at

$0/MW-day in the Third Incremental Auction.33 If the final Accredited UCAP is less than the

amount considered in the Base Residual Auction or the RMR Resource no longer qualifies, the

Office of the Interconnection will seek additional capacity commitments equivalent to the

Unforced Capacity shortfall through the Third Incremental Auction.34 The cleared Unforced

Capacity of an RMR Resource will be counted toward PJM’s Final RTO Unforced Capacity

Obligation, subject to reductions if the final Accredited UCAP is less than the amount counted in

the Base Residual Auction or the RMR Resource no longer meets the requirements of Tariff,

Attachment DD, section 5.3(b)(i).35 RMR Resources will not be subject to the rights and

obligations of a committed Capacity Resource, nor will they be subject to Non-Performance

Charges or bonus payments.36 All capacity market revenues associated with the cleared Unforced

Capacity of the RMR Resource will be credited to the entities paying for the RMR Resource’s

continuing operations until those operations end or the rate schedule terminates, and any capacity

 market revenues remaining thereafter will be distributed to the Load-Serving Entities that paid the

related reliability charges.37

            Any claims that RMR Resources under the RMR Agreement do not provide the same

amount of capacity service as other committed capacity resources must fail. The Commission has

already determined, notwithstanding the lack of a must-offer requirement or exposure to penalties

arising under the RPM, that an RMR Resource satisfying certain criteria, including the

requirements of Tariff, Attachment DD, section 5.3(b)(i)(A) and (B), “can be expected to perform

similar to a capacity resource such that excluding it from the capacity market supply stack would

result in PJM over-procuring capacity.”38 As the Commission explained,

            We agree with PJM that taking into consideration the resource adequacy
            contributions of RMR resources that meet certain criteria, such that they can be
            reasonably expected to perform, similar to capacity resources, will reflect the actual
            availability of resources in the PJM Region for the 2026/2027 and 2027/2028
            delivery years and avoid the risk that load will pay twice for the same capacity.39

Indeed, the Commission “has, in fact, found that doing otherwise would result in customers paying

for more capacity than they need.”40 Further, the Commission determined that the obligation in

Tariff, Attachment DD, section 5.3(b)(i)(B) “demonstrates that a qualifying RMR resource will be

a reasonable substitute for a capacity resource in terms of its ability to contribute to resource

adequacy during emergencies.”41

                                                     19
        B.      Updates to Tariff, Part V, Sections 113.2 and 113.3

       Under the Proposed Revisions, after receiving a notification from PJM that Deactivation

of a Generation Owner’s generating unit would raise reliability concerns, a Generation Owner that

agrees to continue operating its generating unit beyond its desired Deactivation Date must execute

the RMR Agreement after consulting with PJM. That Generation Owner will be entitled to file a

cost-of-service rate with the Commission pursuant to FPA section 205 to recover the entire cost of

operating the generating unit until Deactivation. The Proposed Revisions further amend Tariff,

Part V, section 113.2 to require the Generation Owner to consult with PJM and execute the RMR

Agreement if it elects, in the alternative, to receive the Deactivation Avoidable Cost Credit.

       PJM also proposes to remove Tariff, Part V, section 113.3 of the Tariff, which outlined the

procedures for a Generation Owner to submit a subsequent Deactivation notice for generating units

that have previously agreed to continue operating beyond their desired Deactivation Date. That

section is no longer applicable because, under the Proposed Revisions, any generating units that

continue to operate beyond the desired Deactivation Date must execute the RMR Agreement,

which governs Generation Owner termination procedures.

       C.      Changes to Tariff, Part V, Section 114

       Tariff, Part V, section 114 is amended to remove the obligation of a Generation Owner

operating an RMR facility to receive a monthly Deactivation Avoidable Cost Credit. Now,

Generation Owners may elect to receive such credits but are not obligated to do so. PJM further

proposes to streamline Tariff, Part V, section 114 by revising it to provide that “a Generation

Owner or its Designated Agent shall be eligible for Deactivation Avoidable Cost Credits for the

term specified in the executed Form Reliability Must Run Service Agreement.” Tariff, Part V,

section 2.1 of the RMR Agreement provides that, absent earlier termination or extension beyond

the term, the term will commence on the Effective Date and end on the Anticipated In-Service



                                                20
 Date of the relevant Transmission Upgrades. PJM further proposes to amend the definition of

Actual Net Revenues to state that:

       To the extent that the Actual Net Revenues exceed the other components of the
       Deactivation Avoidable Cost Credit, yielding a monthly Deactivation Avoidable
       Cost Credit less than $0, the Deactivation Avoidable Cost Credit shall be $0. The
       difference between the Actual Net Revenues and all other components of the credit
       shall carry forward and be added to the following month’s Actual Net Revenues.
       If, at the conclusion of the term specified in the executed Form Reliability Must
       Run Service Agreement under Tariff, Part V, Subpart A, the Actual Net Revenues
       for the entire term exceed the summation of the other components of the credit for
       the entire term, the generating unit owner shall retain the excess Actual Net
       Revenues.

       D.      Changes to Tariff, Part V, Section 118

       PJM proposes to amend Tariff, Part V, section 118 to reflect that the generating unit may

remain operational beyond “the term specified in the executed Form Reliability Must Run Service

Agreement under Tariff, Part V, Subpart A,” similar to the Proposed Revisions to Section 114.

       E.      Changes to Tariff, Part V, Section 119

       Tariff, Part V, section 119 has been amended to include reference to the RMR Agreement

by stating that a Generation Owner with a generating unit proposed for Deactivation that continues

operating beyond the proposed Deactivation Date and “executes the Form Reliability Must Run

Service Agreement under Tariff, Part V, Subpart A” may file a cost of service rate with the

Commission.

       F.      Changes to Tariff, Part V, Section 121

       Tariff, Part V, section 121 has been amended to include reference to the RMR Agreement

by requiring a generating unit proposed for Deactivation that continues to operate for reliability

beyond the desired Deactivation Date to operate in accordance with PJM’s existing standards “and

in accordance with the executed Form Reliability Must Run Service Agreement under Tariff, Part

V, Subpart A.”

 V.         EFFECTIVE DATE

           PJM requests that the Commission accept the new RMR Agreement and the Proposed

Revisions effective December 15, 2026.            PJM also respectfully requests that the Commission

issue an order accepting this filing, without condition or modification, on or before December 14,

PJM Open Access Transmission Tariff


         (Marked Format)
 113    Notices

113.1 Generation Owner Notice:

When a Generation Owner desires to deactivate a generating unit located in the PJM Region,
such Generation Owner, or its Designated Agent, must provide notice of such proposed
Deactivation in writing to the Transmission Provider at least twelve (12) months prior to the
desired Deactivation Date. This notice shall include an indication of whether the generating unit
is being retired or mothballed, the desired Deactivation Date, and, if mothballing, a good faith
estimate of the time period the generating unit would be out of service. The desired Deactivation
Date may be no earlier than the following: (a) April 1 of the following calendar year, if the
Transmission Provider receives the notice between January 1 and March 31; (b) July 1 of the
following calendar year, if the Transmission Provider receives the notice between April 1 and
June 30; (c) October 1 of the following calendar year, if the Transmission Provider receives the
notice between July 1 and September 30; or (d) January 1 of the second calendar year, if the
Transmission Provider receives the notice between October 1 and December 31. The
Transmission Provider shall promptly provide a copy of such notice to the Market Monitoring
Unit. The desired Deactivation Date may be earlier than the above-referenced dates if the
Generation Owner, or its Designated Agent, (i) receives notice from a state or federal regulatory
entity that requires or compels the Generation Owner, as a matter of law, to deactivate its
generating unit by a date earlier than the dates permitted by this Tariff, Part V, section 113.1 (ii)
receives such notice on a date that renders compliance with this provision infeasible; and (iii) the
generating unit experiences a catastrophic failure as reasonably determined by the Transmission
Provider which renders compliance with this provision infeasible.

113.2 Notice of Reliability Impact:

The Transmission Provider shall inform the Generation Owner, or its Designated Agent, whether
the Deactivation of the generating unit would adversely affect the reliability of the Transmission
System (“Notice of Reliability Impact”) by the following date: (a) May 31 of the current
calendar year, if the Transmission Provider received the notice required pursuant to Tariff, Part
V, section 113.1 between January 1 and March 31; (b) August 31 of the current calendar year, if
the Transmission Provider received the notice required pursuant to Tariff, Part V, section 113.1
between April 1 and June 30; (c) November 30 of the current calendar year, if the Transmission
Provider received the notice required pursuant to Tariff, Part V, section 113.1 between July 1 and
September 30; or (d) February 28 of the following calendar year, if the Transmission Provider
received the notice required pursuant to Tariff, Part V, section 113.1 between October 1 and
December 31. In the event there are no reliability issues associated with the proposed
Deactivation of the generating unit, the Notice of Reliability Impact shall so notify the
Generation Owner, or its Designated Agent, and the Generation Owner or its Designated Agent
may deactivate its generating unit at any time thereafter. The Generation Owner shall coordinate
with the appropriate Transmission Owner and the Transmission Provider regarding the removal
of any transmission equipment located at the generating unit proposed for Deactivation. In the
event the Transmission Provider determines that, in accordance with established reliability
criteria, the Deactivation of the Generation Owner’s generating unit would adversely affect the
reliability of the Transmission System absent upgrades to the Transmission System, the Notice of



                                                                                               Page 1
 Reliablity Impact shall notify the Generation Owner, or its Designated Agent, of the reliability
concerns. Such Notice of Reliablity Impact shall (1) identify the specific reliability impact
resulting from the proposed Deactivation of the generating unit; and (2) provide an initial
estimate of the period of time it will take to complete the Transmission System reliability
upgrades necessary to alleviate the reliability impact. Regardless of whether the Deactivation of
the generating unit would adversely affect the reliability of the Transmission System, the
Generation Owner or its Designated Agent may deactivate its generating unit, subject to the
notice requirements in Tariff, Part V, section 113.1. Within 30 days of the Generation Owner’s
or its Designated Agent’s receipt of the Notice of Reliability Impact identifying reliability
concerns pursuant to this Tariff, Part V, section 113.2, the Generation Owner or its Designated
Agent shall inform Transmission Provider whether the generating unit proposed for Deactivation
will continue operating beyond its desired Deactivation Date during the period of construction of
the Transmission System reliability upgrades necessary to alleviate the reliability impact
resulting from the Deactivation of the generating unit, and if the generating unit will continue
operating, provide the Transmission Provider with an estimate of the amount of any project
investment and the time period the generating unit would be out of service for repairs, if any, that
would be required to keep the unit in, or return the unit to, operation. For generating units that
will continue operating beyond their desired Deactivation Dates, the Transmission Provider shall
(a) within 45 days of the Transmission Provider issuing the Notice of Reliability Impact pursuant
to this Tariff, Part V, section 113.2, provide an updated estimate of the period of time it will take
to complete the Transmission System upgrades necessary to alleviate the reliability impact; and
(b) within 60 days of the Transmission Provider issuing the Notice of Reliability Impact pursuant
to this Tariff, Part V, section 113.2, post on its internet site full details of the transmission
upgrades necessary to alleviate the reliability impact that would result from the Deactivation of
the generating unit. Upon receipt of notification from the Transmission Provider that
Deactivation of the generating unit would cause reliability concerns, the Generation Owner that
agrees to continue operating its generating unit beyond its desired Deactivation Date shall, after
consultation with the Transmission Provider, execute the Form Reliability Must Run Service
Agreement under Tariff, Part V, Subpart A, and immediately be entitled to file with the
Commission a cost of service rate to recover the entire cost of operating the generating unit until
such time as the generating unit is deactivated pursuant to this Part V (“Cost of Service Recovery
Rate”). In the alternative, the Generation Owner may elect to receive the Deactivation
Avoidable Cost Credit provided under this Part V, after consultation with the Transmission
Provider and execution of the Form Reliability Must Run Service Agreement under Tariff, Part
V, Subpart A.

113.3 Subsequent Deactivation Notice for Generating Units Continuing to Operate:

In the event that a Generation Owner or its Designated Agent, which has informed Transmission
Provider pursuant to section 113.2 that a generating unit will continue operating, desires to
deactivate such generating unit prior to the completion date of the Transmission System
reliability upgrades necessary to alleviate the reliability impact resulting from the Deactivation of
the generating unit, or the date that the Transmission Provider otherwise determines, in
accordance with established reliability criteria, that the continued operation of the generating unit
is no longer necessary for the reliability of the Transmission System, the Generation Owner or its
Designated Agent shall provide notice of such proposed Deactivation in writing to the



                                                                                               Page 2
 Transmission Provider no later than 90 days prior to the desired Deactivation Date for the
generating unit.

113.43 Notice for Generation Units Providing Reactive Supply and Voltage Control:

In addition to the notice requirements in this Tariff, Part V, when a Generation Owner desires to
deactivate a generating unit that provides reactive supply and voltage control service under
Tariff, Schedule 2, such Generation Owner, or its Designated Agent, must satisfy the notice and
filing requirements in Tariff, Schedule 2.




                                                                                           Page 3
 114      Deactivation Avoidable Cost Credit:

In the event that the Generation Owner or its Designated Agent informs Transmission Provider
pursuant to section 113.2 that it will continue operating a generating unit beyond its desired
Deactivation Date, the Generation Owner or its Designated Agent shallmay elect to receive a
monthly Deactivation Avoidable Cost Credit for such continued operation pursuant to the terms
and conditions of this section 114.

         Subject to section 119 of this Tariff, a Generation Owner or its Designated Agent shall be
         eligible for Deactivation Avoidable Cost Credits for the term specified in the executed
         Form Reliability Must Run Service Agreement under Tariff, Part V, Subpart
         A.commencing on the later of the proposed Deactivation Date of its generating unit or the
         day after the Generation Owner or its Designated Agent submits the informational filing
         pursuant to section 116 of this Tariff and continuing until the earlier of such time as the
         generating unit is deactivated or the completion date of the necessary

         Transmission System reliability upgrades that would alleviate the reliability impact
         resulting from the Deactivation of the generating unit, or the Transmission Provider
         otherwise determines, in accordance with established reliability criteria, that the
         continued operation of the generating unit is no longer necessary for the reliability of the
         Transmission System. The Transmission Provider shall give at least thirty days notice to
         a Generation Owner or its Designated Agent of the date when continued operation of a
         generating unit is no longer required under Part V of the Tariff.

         Deactivation Avoidable Cost Credits shall be determined according to the following
         formula:

         Deactivation Avoidable Cost Credit = ((Deactivation Avoidable Cost Rate *
         Applicable Multiplier) * MW capability of the unit * Number of days in the
         month) + (APIR * First Year Multiplier) – Actual Net Revenues

Where:

         Deactivation Avoidable Cost Rate is the Generation Owner’s Deactivation Avoidable
         Cost Rate determined pursuant to section 115 of this Tariff.

Applicable Adder is the appropriate multiplier specified below:

         First Year Multiplier: 110 percent. This multiplier shall apply commencing on the
         desired Deactivation Date of the generating unit proposed for Deactivation and for the 12
         months thereafter.

         Second Year Multiplier: 120 percent. This multiplier shall apply commencing on the
         first day of the 13th month after the desired Deactivation Date of the generating unit
         proposed for Deactivation and for the 12 months thereafter.




                                                                                               Page 4
        Third Year Multiplier: 135 percent. This multiplier shall apply commencing on the
       first day of the 25th month after the desired Deactivation Date of the generating unit
       proposed for Deactivation and for the 12 months thereafter.

       Fourth Year Multiplier: 150 percent. This multiplier shall apply commencing on the
       first day of the 37th month after the desired Deactivation Date of the generating unit
       proposed for Deactivation and until the earlier of such time as the generating unit is
       deactivated or the completion date of the necessary Transmission System reliability
       upgrades that would alleviate the reliability impact resulting from the Deactivation of the
       generating unit, or the Transmission Provider otherwise determines, in accordance with
       established reliability criteria, that the continued operation of the generating unit is no
       longer necessary for the reliability of the Transmission System.

(Deactivation Avoidable Cost Rate * Applicable Multiplier) is expressed in $/MW day.

Actual Net Revenues are all revenues from PJM markets and unit-specific bilateral contracts net
of marginal cost of service recoverable under cost-based offers to sell energy from operating
capacity on the PJM Interchange Energy Market under the Operating Agreement, not less than
zero.

To the extent that the Actual Net Revenues exceed the other components of the Deactivation
Avoidable Cost Credit, yielding a monthly Deactivation Avoidable Cost Credit less than $0, the
Deactivation Avoidable Cost Credit shall be $0. The difference between the Actual Net
Revenues and all other components of the credit shall carry forward and be added to the
following month’s Actual Net Revenues. If, at the conclusion of the term specified in the
executed Form Reliability Must Run Service Agreement under Tariff, Part V, Subpart A, the
Actual Net Revenues for the entire term exceed the summation of the other components of the
credit for the entire term, the generating unit owner shall retain the excess Actual Net
Revenues.Deactivation Avoidable Cost Credit shall not be less than zero.

The Market Monitoring Unit and the generating unit owner shall attempt to come to agreement
on the appropriate level of each component included in the Deactivation Avoidable Cost Credit.
If a generating unit owner includes a cost component inconsistent with its agreement or
inconsistent with the Market Monitoring Unit’s determination regarding such cost components,
the Market Monitoring Unit may petition the Commission for an order that would require the
generating unit owner to include an appropriate cost component. This provision is duplicated in
section IV.2 of Attachment M – Appendix.




                                                                                            Page 5
 118      Refund of Project Investment Reimbursement:

In the event that the Generation Owner’s PI in the generating unit proposed for Deactivation and
credited through the APIR set forth in Tariff, Part V, section 115 enables the generating unit to
remain operational beyond the completion date of the necessary Transmission System reliability
upgrades that would alleviate the reliability impact resulting from the Deactivation of the
generating unit, or the date that the Transmission Provider otherwise determines, in accordance
with established reliability criteria, that the continued operation of the generating unit is no
longer necessary for the reliability of the Transmission Systemthe term specified in the executed
Form Reliability Must Run Service Agreement under Tariff, Part V, Subpart A, and the
generating unit remains in service beyond such date, the Generation Owner or its Designated
Agent shall refund Transmission Provider a pro-rata share of the amount of any PI for which it
received reimbursement pursuant to the APIR set forth in Tariff, Part V, section 115. The
Refund of Project Investment Reimbursement shall be determined using the following formula:

Refund of Project Investment Reimbursement = ((Number of months the PI permits the
generating unit proposed for Deactivation to operate – The number of months Transmission
Provider determines is required to construct the Transmission System reliability upgrades
necessary to alleviate the reliability impact resulting from the Deactivation of the generating
unit) / (Number of months the PI permits the generating unit proposed for Deactivation to
operate)) * (The amount of the PI/ (Number of months the PI allows the generating unit
proposed for Deactivation to continue to operate past the completion date of the necessary
Transmission System reliability upgrades that would alleviate the reliability impact resulting
from the Deactivation of the generating unit, or the date that the Transmission Provider
otherwise determines, in accordance with established reliability criteria, that the continued
operation of the generating unit is no longer necessary for the reliability of the Transmission
System)).

Where:

The number of months the PI permits the generating unit proposed for Deactivation to
operate is determined by the Generation Owner or its Designated Agent and verified by an
independent entity.

Generation Owner or its Designated Agent shall make the Refund of Project Investment
Reimbursement each month for the number of months the PI allows the generating unit proposed
for Deactivation to continue to operate past the completion date of the necessary Transmission
System reliability upgrades that would alleviate the reliability impact resulting from the
Deactivation of the generating unit, or the date that the Transmission Provider otherwise
determines, in accordance with established reliability criteria, that the continued operation of the
generating unit is no longer necessary for the reliability of the Transmission System and shall be
credited to transmission customers in such month on the same basis as costs are allocated under
section 120. The months the generating unit proposed for Deactivation continues to operate past
the completion date of the necessary Transmission System reliability upgrades that would
alleviate the reliability impact resulting from the Deactivation of the generating unit, or the date
that the Transmission Provider otherwise determines, in accordance with established reliability


                                                                                              Page 6
 criteria, that the continued operation of the generating unit is no longer necessary for the
reliability of the Transmission System need not be continuous, and the Refund of Project
Investment Reimbursement will continue regardless of ownership of the generating unit.




                                                                                      Page 7
 119    Cost of Service Recovery Rate:

Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in Part V of this Tariff, a Generation Owner with a
generating unit proposed for Deactivation that continues operating beyond its proposed
Deactivation Date and executes the Form Reliability Must Run Service Agreement under Tariff,
Part V, Subpart A may file with the Commission a cost of service rate to recover the entire cost
of operating the generating unit until such time as the generating unit is deactivated pursuant to
this Part V (“Cost of Service Recovery Rate”). In the event that the Generation Owner or its
Designated Agent files a rate pursuant to this section 119, the Generation Owner shall not be
eligible to receive Deactivation Avoidable Cost Credits, except as provided pursuant to this
section 119, and PJMSettlement shall pay the Generation Owner the Cost of Service Recovery
Rate accepted by the Commission commencing on the effective date established by the
Commission for the rate. In the event the Generation Owner or its Designated Agent already is
receiving Deactivation Avoidable Cost Credits, prior to filing an Cost of Service Recovery Rate,
such Deactivation Avoidable Cost Credits will cease as of the date that the Generation Owner or
its Designated Agent files its Cost of Service Recovery Rate, and PJMSettlement shall begin
paying the Generation Owner or its Designated Agent the Cost of Service Recovery Rate
accepted by the Commission commencing on the effective date established by the Commission
for the rate.

A generating resource owner shall direct all inquiries regarding avoidable expenses to the Market
Monitoring Unit. If a generating resource owner includes a cost component inconsistent with its
agreement or inconsistent with the Market Monitoring Unit’s determination regarding such cost
components, the Market Monitoring Unit may petition the Commission for an order that would
require the generating resource owner to include an appropriate cost component. This provision
is duplicated in section IV.2 of Attachment M – Appendix.




                                                                                             Page 8
 121    Performance Standards:

A generating unit proposed for Deactivation that continues to operate for reliability beyond its
desired Deactivation Date pursuant to Part V of the Tariff shall continue to be operated
according to existing standards applicable to generating units located in the PJM Region and in
accordance with the executed Form Reliability Must Run Service Agreement under Tariff, Part
V, Subpart A.

NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants herein contained, together with

acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:




                                                                                            Page 12
                                        SECTION 1
                                      DEFINITIONS

1.0   Definitions

 113    Notices

113.1 Generation Owner Notice:

When a Generation Owner desires to deactivate a generating unit located in the PJM Region, such
Generation Owner, or its Designated Agent, must provide notice of such proposed Deactivation in
writing to the Transmission Provider at least twelve (12) months prior to the desired Deactivation
Date. This notice shall include an indication of whether the generating unit is being retired or
mothballed, the desired Deactivation Date, and, if mothballing, a good faith estimate of the time
period the generating unit would be out of service. The desired Deactivation Date may be no
earlier than the following: (a) April 1 of the following calendar year, if the Transmission Provider
receives the notice between January 1 and March 31; (b) July 1 of the following calendar year, if
the Transmission Provider receives the notice between April 1 and June 30; (c) October 1 of the
following calendar year, if the Transmission Provider receives the notice between July 1 and
September 30; or (d) January 1 of the second calendar year, if the Transmission Provider receives
the notice between October 1 and December 31. The Transmission Provider shall promptly
provide a copy of such notice to the Market Monitoring Unit. The desired Deactivation Date may
be earlier than the above-referenced dates if the Generation Owner, or its Designated Agent, (i)
receives notice from a state or federal regulatory entity that requires or compels the Generation
Owner, as a matter of law, to deactivate its generating unit by a date earlier than the dates permitted
by this Tariff, Part V, section 113.1 (ii) receives such notice on a date that renders compliance with
this provision infeasible; and (iii) the generating unit experiences a catastrophic failure as
reasonably determined by the Transmission Provider which renders compliance with this provision
infeasible.

113.2 Notice of Reliability Impact:

The Transmission Provider shall inform the Generation Owner, or its Designated Agent, whether
the Deactivation of the generating unit would adversely affect the reliability of the Transmission
System (“Notice of Reliability Impact”) by the following date: (a) May 31 of the current calendar
year, if the Transmission Provider received the notice required pursuant to Tariff, Part V, section
113.1 between January 1 and March 31; (b) August 31 of the current calendar year, if the
Transmission Provider received the notice required pursuant to Tariff, Part V, section 113.1
between April 1 and June 30; (c) November 30 of the current calendar year, if the Transmission
Provider received the notice required pursuant to Tariff, Part V, section 113.1 between July 1 and
September 30; or (d) February 28 of the following calendar year, if the Transmission Provider
received the notice required pursuant to Tariff, Part V, section 113.1 between October 1 and
December 31. In the event there are no reliability issues associated with the proposed Deactivation
of the generating unit, the Notice of Reliability Impact shall so notify the Generation Owner, or its
Designated Agent, and the Generation Owner or its Designated Agent may deactivate its
generating unit at any time thereafter. The Generation Owner shall coordinate with the appropriate
Transmission Owner and the Transmission Provider regarding the removal of any transmission
equipment located at the generating unit proposed for Deactivation. In the event the Transmission
Provider determines that, in accordance with established reliability criteria, the Deactivation of the
Generation Owner’s generating unit would adversely affect the reliability of the Transmission
System absent upgrades to the Transmission System, the Notice of Reliablity Impact shall notify



                                                                                                 Page 1
 the Generation Owner, or its Designated Agent, of the reliability concerns. Such Notice of
Reliablity Impact shall (1) identify the specific reliability impact resulting from the proposed
Deactivation of the generating unit; and (2) provide an initial estimate of the period of time it will
take to complete the Transmission System reliability upgrades necessary to alleviate the reliability
impact. Regardless of whether the Deactivation of the generating unit would adversely affect the
reliability of the Transmission System, the Generation Owner or its Designated Agent may
deactivate its generating unit, subject to the notice requirements in Tariff, Part V, section 113.1.
Within 30 days of the Generation Owner’s or its Designated Agent’s receipt of the Notice of
Reliability Impact identifying reliability concerns pursuant to this Tariff, Part V, section 113.2, the
Generation Owner or its Designated Agent shall inform Transmission Provider whether the
generating unit proposed for Deactivation will continue operating beyond its desired Deactivation
Date during the period of construction of the Transmission System reliability upgrades necessary
to alleviate the reliability impact resulting from the Deactivation of the generating unit, and if the
generating unit will continue operating, provide the Transmission Provider with an estimate of the
amount of any project investment and the time period the generating unit would be out of service

 113    Notices

113.1 Generation Owner Notice:

When a Generation Owner desires to deactivate a generating unit located in the PJM Region, such
Generation Owner, or its Designated Agent, must provide notice of such proposed Deactivation in
writing to the Transmission Provider at least twelve (12) months prior to the desired Deactivation
Date. This notice shall include an indication of whether the generating unit is being retired or
mothballed, the desired Deactivation Date, and, if mothballing, a good faith estimate of the time
period the generating unit would be out of service. The desired Deactivation Date may be no
earlier than the following: (a) April 1 of the following calendar year, if the Transmission Provider
receives the notice between January 1 and March 31; (b) July 1 of the following calendar year, if
the Transmission Provider receives the notice between April 1 and June 30; (c) October 1 of the
following calendar year, if the Transmission Provider receives the notice between July 1 and
September 30; or (d) January 1 of the second calendar year, if the Transmission Provider receives
the notice between October 1 and December 31. The Transmission Provider shall promptly
provide a copy of such notice to the Market Monitoring Unit. The desired Deactivation Date may
be earlier than the above-referenced dates if the Generation Owner, or its Designated Agent, (i)
receives notice from a state or federal regulatory entity that requires or compels the Generation
Owner, as a matter of law, to deactivate its generating unit by a date earlier than the dates permitted
by this Tariff, Part V, section 113.1 (ii) receives such notice on a date that renders compliance with
this provision infeasible; and (iii) the generating unit experiences a catastrophic failure as
reasonably determined by the Transmission Provider which renders compliance with this provision
infeasible.

113.2 Notice of Reliability Impact:

The Transmission Provider shall inform the Generation Owner, or its Designated Agent, whether
the Deactivation of the generating unit would adversely affect the reliability of the Transmission
System (“Notice of Reliability Impact”) by the following date: (a) May 31 of the current calendar
year, if the Transmission Provider received the notice required pursuant to Tariff, Part V, section
113.1 between January 1 and March 31; (b) August 31 of the current calendar year, if the
Transmission Provider received the notice required pursuant to Tariff, Part V, section 113.1
between April 1 and June 30; (c) November 30 of the current calendar year, if the Transmission
Provider received the notice required pursuant to Tariff, Part V, section 113.1 between July 1 and
September 30; or (d) February 28 of the following calendar year, if the Transmission Provider
received the notice required pursuant to Tariff, Part V, section 113.1 between October 1 and
December 31. In the event there are no reliability issues associated with the proposed Deactivation
of the generating unit, the Notice of Reliability Impact shall so notify the Generation Owner, or its
Designated Agent, and the Generation Owner or its Designated Agent may deactivate its
generating unit at any time thereafter. The Generation Owner shall coordinate with the appropriate
Transmission Owner and the Transmission Provider regarding the removal of any transmission
equipment located at the generating unit proposed for Deactivation. In the event the Transmission
Provider determines that, in accordance with established reliability criteria, the Deactivation of the
Generation Owner’s generating unit would adversely affect the reliability of the Transmission
System absent upgrades to the Transmission System, the Notice of Reliablity Impact shall notify
 the Generation Owner, or its Designated Agent, of the reliability concerns. Such Notice of
Reliablity Impact shall (1) identify the specific reliability impact resulting from the proposed
Deactivation of the generating unit; and (2) provide an initial estimate of the period of time it will
take to complete the Transmission System reliability upgrades necessary to alleviate the reliability
impact. Regardless of whether the Deactivation of the generating unit would adversely affect the
reliability of the Transmission System, the Generation Owner or its Designated Agent may
deactivate its generating unit, subject to the notice requirements in Tariff, Part V, section 113.1.
Within 30 days of the Generation Owner’s or its Designated Agent’s receipt of the Notice of
Reliability Impact identifying reliability concerns pursuant to this Tariff, Part V, section 113.2, the
Generation Owner or its Designated Agent shall inform Transmission Provider whether the
generating unit proposed for Deactivation will continue operating beyond its desired Deactivation
Date during the period of construction of the Transmission System reliability upgrades necessary
to alleviate the reliability impact resulting from the Deactivation of the generating unit, and if the
generating unit will continue operating, provide the Transmission Provider with an estimate of the
amount of any project investment and the time period the generating unit would be out of service
for repairs, if any, that would be required to keep the unit in, or return the unit to, operation. For
generating units that will continue operating beyond their desired Deactivation Dates, the
Transmission Provider shall (a) within 45 days of the Transmission Provider issuing the Notice of
Reliability Impact pursuant to this Tariff, Part V, section 113.2, provide an updated estimate of the
period of time it will take to complete the Transmission System upgrades necessary to alleviate the
reliability impact; and (b) within 60 days of the Transmission Provider issuing the Notice of
Reliability Impact pursuant to this Tariff, Part V, section 113.2, post on its internet site full details
of the transmission upgrades necessary to alleviate the reliability impact that would result from the
Deactivation of the generating unit. Upon receipt of notification from the Transmission Provider
that Deactivation of the generating unit would cause reliability concerns, the Generation Owner
that agrees to continue operating its generating unit beyond its desired Deactivation Date shall,
after consultation with the Transmission Provider, execute the Form Reliability Must Run Service
Agreement under Tariff, Part V, Subpart A, and immediately be entitled to file with the
Commission a cost of service rate to recover the entire cost of operating the generating unit until
such time as the generating unit is deactivated pursuant to this Part V (“Cost of Service Recovery
Rate”). In the alternative, the Generation Owner may elect to receive the Deactivation Avoidable
Cost Credit provided under this Part V, after consultation with the Transmission Provider and
execution of the Form Reliability Must Run Service Agreement under Tariff, Part V, Subpart A.


113.3 Notice for Generation Units Providing Reactive Supply and Voltage Control:

In addition to the notice requirements in this Tariff, Part V, when a Generation Owner desires to
deactivate a generating unit that provides reactive supply and voltage control service under Tariff,
Schedule 2, such Generation Owner, or its Designated Agent, must satisfy the notice and filing
requirements in Tariff, Schedule 2.

 114      Deactivation Avoidable Cost Credit:

In the event that the Generation Owner or its Designated Agent informs Transmission Provider
pursuant to section 113.2 that it will continue operating a generating unit beyond its desired
Deactivation Date, the Generation Owner or its Designated Agent may elect to receive a monthly
Deactivation Avoidable Cost Credit for such continued operation pursuant to the terms and
conditions of this section 114.

         Subject to section 119 of this Tariff, a Generation Owner or its Designated Agent shall be
         eligible for Deactivation Avoidable Cost Credits for the term specified in the executed
         Form Reliability Must Run Service Agreement under Tariff, Part V, Subpart A.
         Deactivation Avoidable Cost Credits shall be determined according to the following
         formula:

         Deactivation Avoidable Cost Credit = ((Deactivation Avoidable Cost Rate *
         Applicable Multiplier) * MW capability of the unit * Number of days in the
         month) + (APIR * First Year Multiplier) – Actual Net Revenues

Where:

         Deactivation Avoidable Cost Rate is the Generation Owner’s Deactivation Avoidable
         Cost Rate determined pursuant to section 115 of this Tariff.

Applicable Adder is the appropriate multiplier specified below:

         First Year Multiplier: 110 percent. This multiplier shall apply commencing on the
         desired Deactivation Date of the generating unit proposed for Deactivation and for the 12
         months thereafter.

         Second Year Multiplier: 120 percent. This multiplier shall apply commencing on the
         first day of the 13th month after the desired Deactivation Date of the generating unit
         proposed for Deactivation and for the 12 months thereafter.

         Third Year Multiplier: 135 percent. This multiplier shall apply commencing on the
         first day of the 25th month after the desired Deactivation Date of the generating unit
         proposed for Deactivation and for the 12 months thereafter.

         Fourth Year Multiplier: 150 percent. This multiplier shall apply commencing on the
         first day of the 37th month after the desired Deactivation Date of the generating unit
         proposed for Deactivation and until the earlier of such time as the generating unit is
         deactivated or the completion date of the necessary Transmission System reliability
         upgrades that would alleviate the reliability impact resulting from the Deactivation of the
         generating unit, or the Transmission Provider otherwise determines, in accordance with
         established reliability criteria, that the continued operation of the generating unit is no
         longer necessary for the reliability of the Transmission System.
 (Deactivation Avoidable Cost Rate * Applicable Multiplier) is expressed in $/MW day.

Actual Net Revenues are all revenues from PJM markets and unit-specific bilateral contracts net
of marginal cost of service recoverable under cost-based offers to sell energy from operating
capacity on the PJM Interchange Energy Market under the Operating Agreement.

To the extent that the Actual Net Revenues exceed the other components of the Deactivation
Avoidable Cost Credit, yielding a monthly Deactivation Avoidable Cost Credit less than $0, the
Deactivation Avoidable Cost Credit shall be $0. The difference between the Actual Net
Revenues and all other components of the credit shall carry forward and be added to the
following month’s Actual Net Revenues. If, at the conclusion of the term specified in the
executed Form Reliability Must Run Service Agreement under Tariff, Part V, Subpart A, the
Actual Net Revenues for the entire term exceed the summation of the other components of the
credit for the entire term, the generating unit owner shall retain the excess Actual Net Revenues.

The Market Monitoring Unit and the generating unit owner shall attempt to come to agreement
on the appropriate level of each component included in the Deactivation Avoidable Cost Credit.
If a generating unit owner includes a cost component inconsistent with its agreement or
inconsistent with the Market Monitoring Unit’s determination regarding such cost components,
the Market Monitoring Unit may petition the Commission for an order that would require the
generating unit owner to include an appropriate cost component. This provision is duplicated in
section IV.2 of Attachment M – Appendix.

pro-rata share of the amount of any PI for which it received reimbursement pursuant to the APIR

otherwise determines, in accordance with established reliability criteria, that the continued
operation of the generating unit is no longer necessary for the reliability of the Transmission

Where:

The number of months the PI permits the generating unit proposed for Deactivation to
operate is determined by the Generation Owner or its Designated Agent and verified by an
independent entity.
